subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB495 — The rule PINS the format: "a floating-point data item in 32-bit basic binary interchange format (binary32) as specified in ISO/IEC 60559:2020, 3.4". .NET `System.Single` IS IEEE 754 binary32, and PicInfo.ClrType maps Usage.FloatBinary32 to `float` with no intermediate; ByteForm is Ieee32 and StorageWidth 4. Measured with the pinned compiler (probe p14, --std 2023): FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH is 4; MOVE 16777217 stores 16777216 - the binary32 rounding of 2**24+1, which a double-backed item would have kept exactly, so the probe discriminates the format rather than merely the width; MOVE 0.1 round-trips as the binary32 nearest. The stored bytes are the interchange encoding: probe p29 reads 1.0 out of a group image as 0x3F 0x80 0x00 0x00. conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/float_binary pins the arithmetic and the 4-byte width with spec-computed expectations, and conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/pb174_float_item_endianness pins the encoding of 1.5 as 0x3FC00000 byte by byte. The COBOL-2014 introduction gate fires below 2014 (COBOL0900 at 85 and 2002 - probe p45 and conformance-test:FloatFamilyTests.BinaryBelowIntroduction_Rejected0900). NOTE 1 of the rule is non-normative (and its "+(2**24 - 1), or 16,777,213" is arithmetically 16,777,215); nothing turns on it. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The binary32 claim is genuinely met for an item declared at its own level - I re-measured it three independent ways rather than reusing the adjudicator's p14: FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH 4; MOVE 16777217 stores 16777216 (the binary32 rounding of 2**24+1, which the FLOAT-BINARY-64 twin in the same program keeps exactly); MOVE 3.4028234E38 stores 3.4028235E+38 and MOVE 1.1754943E-38 stores 1.1754944E-38, i.e. the binary32 max and smallest-normal, and MOVE 1.0E-45 survives as a subnormal rather than flushing to zero (which a decimal-backed path would not); and the group image of 1.0 reads 0x3F 0x80 0x00 0x00, the big-endian binary32 interchange encoding. What the CONFORMS verdict does not cover is the declaration shape in which the phrase is inherited. SS13.18.60.4 GR1 (cite-checked) makes a USAGE clause specified at a group level apply to each elementary item in the group, and the compiler accepts `01 GS USAGE FLOAT-BINARY-32.  05 AS2.` with NO diagnostic and exit 0 - but AS2's FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH is 0: the phrase specified nothing, where the rule says it 'specifies that the data item IS a floating-point data item in 32-bit basic binary interchange format'. The same program's SS13.18.60.3 SR2 form (`05 AL USAGE FLOAT-BINARY-64.` under a FLOAT-BINARY-64 group) gives 8, and `01 GI USAGE INDEX.  05 AI.` gives 8, so the group USAGE clause IS accepted and the picture-less resolution machinery exists - it was built for USAGE INDEX only. A MOVE into such an item crashes the compiler (unhandled NullReferenceException, MoveEmitter.ConvertSource) instead of being diagnosed. HONEST CAVEAT on this one: SS13.16.3 SR8's picture-forbidden list names float-short/-long/-extended but NOT the standard binary floating-point usages, so whether an elementary FLOAT-BINARY-32 item may be PICTURE-less rests on the compiler's own (sane, and universally shared) reading rather than on SR8's letter - the spec basis here is weaker than for GR12/GR13/GR21, though the compiler has already committed to that reading by accepting `01 F32 USAGE FLOAT-BINARY-32.`. SECOND, INDEPENDENT GROUND: the cited test does not pin this rule's distinguishing branch. conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/float_binary is spec-derived, but every value in it (10.5, 100.25, and their integer products) is EXACTLY representable in both binary32 and binary64, so it discriminates only the WIDTH, not the FORMAT - a 4-byte non-IEEE float would pass it unchanged. The rounding evidence that actually separates binary32 from binary64 exists only as a probe. NOTE FOR THE REGISTRAR: the inheritance defect is ONE root cause shared with my GR12, GR13, GR15 and GR21 verdicts. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/PictureAnalyzer.cs#PictureAnalyzer.ParseUsage; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.ClrType; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.ByteForm; src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolFloat.cs || CLOSED 2026-09-09 by kb/Work PB495 (landed). The REFUTED paragraph above names the ONE root it shares with GR13, GR14, GR15 and GR21 -- "picture-less group-usage inheritance implemented for INDEX only" -- and says in terms that one fix closes all five. That fix is landed: 13.18.60.4 GR1 is now implemented as an EQUIVALENCE rather than as a special case, over ONE derivation of an elementary item's effective usage (its own USAGE clause, else the nearest enclosing one) feeding the group-header shed, the leaf's representation and every 13.18.60.3 screen through the same code the written-clause path runs. So `01 GB USAGE BINARY-SHORT. 05 AB.` is a 2-byte binary item and `01 GF USAGE FLOAT-LONG. 05 AL.` an 8-byte floating-point one, not the ZERO-LENGTH cells measured above, and the MOVE that crashed the compiler with an unhandled NullReferenceException in MoveEmitter.ConvertSource runs. RE-MEASURED, both spellings, whole matrix: a (usage x picture x arm) sweep of 138 cells found 108 DIFFERING on the pre-fix tree 39479e19 and 0 differing after, and the equivalence is now a drift theory over the whole Usage enum rather than a set of cases. The spec-derived witnesses are the two new goldens: conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/pb495_group_usage_applies_to_each_leaf prints W=1 2 4 8 4 8 8 (binary-char/-short/-long/-double, float-short, float-long, index) with GRP=4 for a two-leaf BINARY-SHORT group and CTL=2 for the written-clause control, and conformance:cases/13.18.60-USAGE/pb495_group_usage_standard_float prints W=4 8 2 2 with F=16777216 16777217 -- 2**24+1 rounded by binary32 and held exactly by binary64, the sharpest single discriminator between the two interchange formats -- and N=-32768 65535, which is GR21 sentence 2's SIGNED/UNSIGNED length identity together with the UNSIGNED phrase reaching the leaf from the group entry. Everything the REFUTED paragraph credits as already holding is unchanged.
